name: GA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals lean Democratic by roughly 25 points
McBath holds an overwhelming fundraising edge ($1.15M raised vs about $10K for Martin)
Renominated incumbent faces a challenger with no outside support or visible campaign resources
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%
model.rationale: A district whose fundamentals favor Democrats by roughly 25 points, a well-funded incumbent, and a challenger who has raised barely ten thousand dollars leave almost no room for competition. Markets and the underlying terrain point the same direction, toward a decisive McBath victory.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary development, such as a major late scandal, McBath leaving the race, or a sudden influx of outside spending for Martin, could put this district in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lucy McBath enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district whose fundamentals now favor Democrats by a wide margin. She secured renomination and holds a commanding financial edge, with about $1.15 million raised and $654,000 on hand, while Republican Kevin Martin has raised roughly $10,000 and reports just $100 remaining. No independent polls are available, and no national ratings organizations have weighed in on the race.

Prediction markets price McBath's chances at about 96 percent, in line with the district's strong Democratic lean. The absence of polling and outside spending on either side suggests the contest has drawn little competitive attention. Barring an unexpected development, McBath's incumbency, resources, and favorable terrain make an upset very difficult to construct, and this race ranks among the least competitive House contests this cycle.
